note: Hints about how an app shares the screen on Wayland. Each names its source; they explain, they never decide a check.

hints.text: Firefox 121 and later run natively on Wayland when a Wayland session is available; older versions run through XWayland unless MOZ_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1 is set.
On Wayland Firefox shares through the portal and needs no extra setting once your desktop's portal backend is installed, so a missing picker points at the portal side.

apps.name: Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Chromium, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi)

hints.text: Chrome and Chromium 110 and later share through PipeWire and the portal by default; older versions need chrome://flags/#enable-webrtc-pipewire-capturer enabled.
Chrome 140 made --ozone-platform-hint=auto the default, so it runs natively on Wayland when available; older versions run through XWayland unless started with that flag.

apps.name: Electron apps (Discord, Slack, Teams for Linux, Signal, VS Code…)

hints.text: With XWayland present, Electron (20 to 22 in this report) captured X11 windows and screens even with PipeWire capture enabled, so only X11 windows could be shared; an app running natively on Wayland gets the portal's picker instead.
Electron 38 and later pick Wayland automatically when it is available (ELECTRON_OZONE_PLATFORM_HINT is deprecated); older Electron apps need --ozone-platform-hint=auto to run natively.

On Wayland OBS captures through its "Screen Capture (PipeWire)" and "Window Capture (PipeWire)" sources, which use the portal; when they are missing from the source list, PipeWire, WirePlumber or the portal are usually not running.

flatpak.text: Flatpak apps cannot read the screen themselves and always share through the portal, so the portal checks apply to them in full.
